title: Scope freeze & release-notes orchestration for API/Console/Runtime release cadence
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: Define and run a repeatable scope-freeze, cut-criteria, and release-notes orchestration process for the combined API / Console / Runtime release cadence. This ticket owns the cross-functional checklist, communications timeline, and release-notes digest responsibilities so engineering, design, docs, and GTM move in lockstep.

Scope: Align milestones across three surfaces (API, Console, Runtime); codify scope-freeze windows; define hard cut criteria for GA vs RC; establish a single release-notes authoring and approval workflow; coordinate customer-facing comms and internal readiness.

Deliverables: 1) Milestone calendar with freeze/cut dates and responsible owners; 2) Cut-criteria matrix (severity gating, test pass thresholds, perf SLOs); 3) Release-notes template and cadence (author, reviewers, publish channel); 4) GTM checklist (blog, changelog, customer emails, sales enablement); 5) Post-release rollout/rollback playbook.

Success metrics: Release notes published within 24 hours of GA; zero critical regressions in first 72 hours post-GA; <10% increase in support volume attributable to unclear notes; all GTM assets delivered by release day.

RACI highlights: PM (Ava Martinez) = overall owner; Release coordinator (Ethan Patel) = day-to-day orchestration; Docs owner (Olivia Park) = release-notes author & publisher; Eng release lead (Diego Ramos) = cut decision authority for runtime; Console design lead (Maya Singh) = UX copy approval; Sales ops (Liam O'Connor) = GTM asset distribution.
acceptance_criteria: Milestone calendar published to Confluence and synced to shared calendar
Cut-criteria matrix documented and signed off by Eng, QA, and Security
Release-notes draft created, reviewed by Docs + Eng, and scheduled for publish
GTM checklist items assigned and >= 90% completed before GA
Rollback steps for runtime and console validated in staging
updates: 2025-11-06: Kickoff meeting with Eng, Docs, Design, Sales. Agreed on single canonical release calendar (Google Calendar + Confluence master page). Action: Ethan to own calendar updates.

2025-11-12: Cut-criteria proposal v1 uploaded. Key trade-off: allow minor UX polish to slip to patch if perf SLOs/critical bugs remain. Decision: prioritize stability for GA; non-blocking UX items move to patch queue.

2025-11-15: Docs owner (Olivia Park) proposed release-notes template including migration notes, breaking changes, and 'What changed for developers' section. Feedback: add example code snippets for API changes. Assigned: DES-412 to produce screenshots.

2025-11-18: Cross-team alignment: agreed scope-freeze window = 2025-11-25 to 2025-12-01; code freeze = 2025-12-03; QA sign-off window ends 2025-12-07. Drafted email to beta customers for early preview (sales ops to review).
2025-11-19: Release notes owner set to Olivia Park. GitHub PR stub created for release-notes draft (https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-notes/pull/212).

2025-11-20: Status -> In Progress. Preparing final cut-criteria for Exec review on 2025-11-24. Added performance SLO thresholds for runtime (p90 token latency < 120ms on dedicated), and API availability target (99.9% for GA).
risks_mitigation: Risk: Runtime perf regression discovered late. Mitigation: build a fast rollback path to previous runtime binary and reserve a rollback slot in Dedicated for 48 hours post-GA.
Risk: Docs lag delaying customer communications. Mitigation: early draft owners assigned; Docs publishes 'preview notes' to internal channel for review two days before code freeze.

Risk: Cross-surface dependency mismatch (API change requires runtime patch). Mitigation: add dependency flagging in milestone calendar and require cross-approval for any surface-altering change after scope-freeze.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Pre-freeze): Establish calendar, owners, and publish pre-release communication templates
Phase 1 (Scope freeze): Block new feature merges across surfaces; urgent bug fixes only with triage and approval
Phase 2 (RC & Docs): Create release candidate build, finalize release-notes, run smoke tests and performance validation
Phase 3 (GA): Publish release notes, update changelog, send customer emails, enable console feature flags for gradual ramp
Phase 4 (Post-GA): Monitor dashboards for 72 hours, run incident playbook if SLOs violated, publish postmortem if severity threshold met
